public_rationale: In February 2026, a simple common-sense question went viral: should you walk or drive to a car wash 50 metres away when you want to wash your car? A systematic test of 53 models found only 5 answered correctly every time, and 33 never did. News coverage of the viral thread found many mainstream models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and xAI failing. Some top models passed, and humans in a 10,000-person baseline also missed it about 28.5% of the time. Still, these documented, reproducible failures support the plain claim that generative AI 'still has problems with common sense'.
limitations: The main systematic test comes from a commercial vendor.
Some frontier models passed reliably, so the claim holds for the field broadly, not for every model.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, widely used generative AI models still often failed simple common-sense questions that humans answer easily.
The example 'circulating on X today' is most likely the viral February 2026 car-wash question, but the claim does not depend on that identification.
Target period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-01, since he points to then-current examples.
criteria.support_condition: Documented, reproducible common-sense failures by then-current mainstream models in early 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Systematic tests in early 2026 show then-current models reliably passing such common-sense questions.

evidence.excerpt: Out of 53 models, only 5 can do this reliably. 15 more can sometimes get there but unpredictably. The remaining 33 never get it right.
evidence.explanation: Most current models failed a trivial common-sense question, repeatedly, in February 2026.

evidence.excerpt: However, only the GPT-5.2 Thinking, Claude Opus 4.6, and Gemini 3 Pro models answered this test correctly.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the failures were widely circulating on X in mid-February 2026, across many mainstream models.

evidence.excerpt: Turns out GPT-5 (7/10) answered about as reliably as the average human (71.5%) in this test.
evidence.explanation: Humans also missed this question about 28.5% of the time, and a few top models passed reliably. This tempers, but does not negate, the finding.
